title: 50 Cent’s 13 Most Memorable Trolling Moments
summary: 50's been trolling long before the term became in vogue.
contentText:
50 Cent is a generational hater. Let’s take it a step further: he’s on the Mount Rushmore of haters. The G-Unit mogul is as petty as they come in beef and there’s no line he won’t cross to make his opps question why they would ever want to feud with him in the first place.

50’s been trolling way before it became a popular term among millennials and part of the DNA of the social media zeitgeist.

In part, his rap career took off because of trolling with his breakout “How to Rob” single in 1999, which found him hypothetically mugging Diddy, Keith Sweat , Mase and Master P. He remains entrenched in a cold war with a few of the “How to Rob” targets decades later, like Jay-Z and Diddy, the latter of whom 50 claims his beef started with after Combs asked to take him shopping.

While 50 isn’t dominating the charts and cooking up club anthems in a bulletproof vest like it’s the mid-2000s, as his focus has switched to his G-Unit Film/TV production company and spirits empire, the Queens icon’s unfiltered opinions still move the needle globally.

Trolling has long been part of the equation in rap beefs, and 50 has the cleverness, audacity and catalog to back it up in battle. 50’s antagonizing antics that landed on his ThisIs50 website were ahead of their time. He’s got a PHD diploma in understanding the internet, and has shown a shrewd ability to evolve in the digital era. At the same time, many of the 50-year-old’s peers would probably pronounce meme incorrectly.

While he seems to take joy in emasculating his opponents, 50 says he doesn’t take his art of war too seriously. “None of that is really personal, it’s just me having fun at the end of the day,” 50 told Hot 97 in 2024.

With victims ranging from Fat Joe to DJ Khaled and Rick Ross, here we recall some of 50 Cent’s most memorable trolling moments over the years.
